summary: A Tal Corvus evacuation queue remains a neighborhood: ordinary arguments, a funny argument about a borrowed kettle, and a small child's drawing make the departure personally specific.
panelPlan: Pre-dawn in the inhabited Tal Corvus warrens: a mother fastens a stubborn heater strap while her daughter stands on a battered crate. Neighbors queue with only what they can carry.
A familiar mechanic accuses the neighbor of borrowing a kettle years ago. Their argument is affectionate but detailed; the mother cannot help laughing, though she keeps checking the departure doors.
The girl looks past the adults toward the dock, draws the silhouette of Gravefire on her blank crate, and asks an ordinary question that brings the adults momentarily back to the departure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: You still have my kettle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: I gave that back in spring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: You gave back a saucepan. A kettle has a spout.

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: You never said the spout was part of the loan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Please don't make me choose who gets the saucepan. I can't carry both of you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Do they know we're coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: They know. Keep your place by me.

settingText: EXT. TAL CORVUS WARRENS / EVACUATION QUEUE — PRE-DAWN

summary: The child records the ships she hopes will help; adults passing the time talk about a very real place they once called home, disagreeing cheerfully over its virtues.
panelPlan: In a cramped waiting shelter, the girl draws different, recognizable ship silhouettes in chalk on the unlettered crate. The neighbor kneels to inspect the drawing while the mother repacks a bag.
A retired dock mechanic recalls an old Tal Corvus bakery that had a warm back room and truly dreadful rolls; the neighbor disputes the memory with surprising passion.
The boarding queue creeps forward. The mother lifts the heavy bag, then sets it down so her daughter can finish the last line of her drawing. The crate remains behind as they move.

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: That's supposed to be a Fleet cruiser? You've made it prettier than the real thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: It's supposed to have room for everybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: There was a bakery up on Furnace Walk. Always warm. Couldn't bake bread to save their lives.

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: Their rolls were excellent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: They used the rolls to prop the doors open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: I liked the jam.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: Nobody's arguing with the jam.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Can we come back for my drawing?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: I hope so.

settingText: INT. TAL CORVUS WARREN SHELTER — PRE-DAWN

summary: Thunderbreak arrives with an imposing Fleet screen, creating simultaneous relief and apprehension among evacuees who have just been joking together.
panelPlan: The established, repaired heavy cruiser Thunderbreak emerges from physical reciprocal transit, escorts dispersing into assigned stations without luminous portal effects.
From a shelter window, the mother, child, and their quarrelsome neighbors watch the ships darken a slice of the sky. Humor stops without any explicit command to stop.
Large civilian-scale view: Gravefire waits at the dock, the third-window beacons remain dark, and the immense Fleet formation hangs over the route; the daughter grips her mother's sleeve.

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: Well. They didn't send a small one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: That's what worries me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Is it ours?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Not exactly.

settingText: EXT. TAL CORVUS ORBIT / EVACUATION QUEUE — DAWN

summary: Acting commander Erin Deka, not the removed Venn, commands Thunderbreak; professional familiarity and an old ship's quirks distinguish her crew from a tactical briefing.
panelPlan: Thunderbreak's repaired command bridge: Acting Commander Deka listens to a familiar vibration beneath the helm while Tactical receives third-window defensive orders.
Deka and Helm exchange a dry, restrained observation about Thunderbreak's worn but dependable machinery. Their station work continues while they speak.

Tactical confirms Venn's tribunal removal remains binding, Deka holds command, and offensive release remains with Admiralty. Deka studies the separate Verge and Shard ships on a plain plotting surface.
Deka orders Thunderbreak's existing armored side turned toward the civilian crossing. The crew execute the maneuver smoothly; the guns remain dark.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: That vibration again?

dialogueInline.speaker: Helm
dialogueInline.text: Only when she's cold, ma'am.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Someone told me we repaired it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Helm
dialogueInline.text: We repaired the rattle. She found a new one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Third-window screen orders received. Weapons release stays with Admiralty. Commodore Venn's removal stands.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Understood. Send her the ship's status when we're clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Helm, give the civilians our armored side. Easy turn. No surprises.

settingText: INT. THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND — DAWN
directionInline: Erin Deka lawfully commands Thunderbreak throughout Issue 4; Venn is removed, absent, and neither restored nor advising the bridge. Command familiarity is between Deka and her Fleet crew, not between independent escorts and Fleet station operators.

Fleet humor remains restrained, technically grounded, and appropriate to rank. Preserve Thunderbreak's established older repaired hull, exact geography and ship design; no unscripted display lettering.

summary: Dominion presses Deka to maintain a credible defensive blockade while she asks the question orders have not answered: what if a civilian craft drifts out of reach?
panelPlan: In the functional Relic Court, Dominion watches the live crossing route while Deka appears on a secured Fleet feed aboard Thunderbreak.
Dominion identifies the defensive screen Deka is expected to maintain; Deka acknowledges its necessity rather than dismissing discipline.
Deka uses an unlettered trajectory display to show a hypothetical powerless civilian tug drifting beyond the line. Neither officer has an easy answer.
Dominion leaves the lawful restriction intact. Deka ends the call, takes a measured breath, and turns to the crew already waiting for her decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: I need that screen intact when the civilians start moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: So do I, Admiral.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Then I expect we understand each other.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: On the route, yes. I'm less certain about a ship that can't stay on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: One rescue could expose every vessel still behind it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: And leaving it would be a decision too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: You hold a Fleet command, Lieutenant. Make sure you can defend whatever you decide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Yes, sir.

settingText: INT. BASTION SPIRE — RELIC COURT / THUNDERBREAK COMMS — DAWN
directionInline: Deka remains Thunderbreak's acting commander, and Dominion's restrictive offensive-fire and blockade orders remain fully binding. The disagreement does not transfer command to Verge or Shard partners.

summary: Abby negotiates protection with two independent, difficult Shard captains; an entertaining dispute about captainly entitlement exposes Billie and Pike before the dangerous disagreements.
panelPlan: On a wind-shorn Tal Corvus gantry above working civilian skiffs, Abby sets down a simple public route sketch. Billie arrives eating the last piece of food from a crew tin; Pike notices immediately.

Pike argues with theatrical sincerity that the captain is entitled to the last piece; Billie disagrees at length while Abby refuses to referee. An almost comfortable exchange reveals how well they know one another.
Abby turns the sketch toward Gravefire's position and explains the civilian no-fire boundary in one plain sentence. Billie's amusement evaporates when Abby calls it a condition rather than a request.
Pike positions his cameras toward Broken Oath; Abby looks him in the eye until he finally checks the skiffs below. The captains leave without pretending they have agreed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: You took the last one. In front of witnesses.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I was hungry in front of witnesses.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: On my ship the last portion goes to the captain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then I'd be hungry on your ship too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: It's a biscuit, Oren. Don't convene a court.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Civilian ships go through here. Nobody fires across their path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You can tell your own crew what to do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I'm telling you what happens to families if you don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: My cameras will have the whole crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Try looking at it without them.

settingText: EXT. TAL CORVUS DOCK GANTRY — DAY

summary: Abby and her sister Tess tease each other as only family can, before Tess realizes she has been placed opposite Billie and refuses to make the evacuation a private feud.
panelPlan: At the dockside maintenance rail, Tess checks a stubborn seam in her repaired Shard flight coat. Abby attempts an awkward but practiced repair while they share the last ordinary minutes before departure.
The sisters argue over who taught the other to fix things; Tess recognizes the route slate Abby is holding and notices that Gravefire is facing Billie's projected approach.
Abby admits she chose Tess for the departure lead and couldn't place Billie. Tess is hurt more by Abby's omission than by the assignment itself.
Tess pockets the slate, adjusts her coat without Abby's help, and walks toward Gravefire while summoning her crew. Abby watches her go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You've made it worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: It's holding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: So is a knot in your hair. Doesn't mean it's a repair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: You taught me that stitch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I taught you half of it. You got impatient.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Hang on. That's Billie's approach opposite mine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I couldn't move her. I need you there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You could've started with that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Would it have changed your answer?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: No. That's what makes it annoying.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I'll bring those people out. Billie can be angry at me afterward.

settingText: EXT. TAL CORVUS — DOCK MAINTENANCE RAIL — DAY

summary: Halev turns Auric's last clear freight hall into heated shelter, in a scene grounded in workers, local memory, and Naomi's impatience with explanations that do not warm anyone.
panelPlan: Halev walks through a freight hall as a dockhand struggles to start a heater bank. He remembers the room as a bustling loading floor and makes a gentle joke with a worker about the old place.
Naomi calls from a freezing Tal Corvus boarding area with an actual family visible behind her. She needles Halev about his promise, not his authority.
The freighters will have nowhere to unload if the hall fills with beds. Halev watches his staff wait, unable to solve both shortages.
He waves the heaters through. Workers begin placing beds on the freight floor as other workers stand beside displaced grain pallets.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dockhand
dialogueInline.text: These units take longer every season.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: So do I. They still expect me to start before dawn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Chris, I've got people boarding in coats they'll sleep in. Tell me the heaters work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: They do. The freight hall is the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: A floor is a floor until somebody has to sleep on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The next grain ship needs that floor. If we fill it with beds, we can't unload.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then when it arrives we can have this argument with warm people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Open the hall. Tell the freight crew I'm coming down to help move the pallets.

settingText: INT. AURIC FREEPORT — FREIGHT HALL / TAL CORVUS COMMS — DAY

summary: Jex surrenders valuable route intelligence to Halev while his wry account of former business highlights both his working life and the conspicuous unanswered contact from Tali.
panelPlan: In the working Veil Market, Jex adjusts his rib bandage and steals a chair from a busy broker who has never willingly lent it. His cramped route desk shows an unanswered personal channel.
Jex and Halev connect by comm. Jex transmits one urgently current three-screen intercept trace, joking about a customer who once disputed an obviously valid bill.
Halev notices that Jex has not charged for this information. The absence of a demand is more alarming than the map itself.
Jex asks Halev to keep looking for missing Tali. Halev gives a simple promise and forwards the warning toward Naomi.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Tell him I'll give the chair back when he stops charging for sitting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Three ships, three separate intercepts. I used to sell information like this to a man who argued over the price of ink.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: And you still sold it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: He paid. He just needed to feel he'd won something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: You're not asking for anything today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Today there's no time to haggle. Get the map to Naomi.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: One more thing. If Tali appears on any arrival list, I want to hear before the lists go public.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I'll call you myself.

settingText: INT. VEIL MARKET — BROKER BALCONY — DAY

summary: Naomi and her Sunlash co-pilot exchange a candid personal opinion while interpreting Jex's warning and placing themselves at the far end of the civilian crossing.
panelPlan: In Sunlash's cramped worn cockpit, the co-pilot drinks something terrible from a reusable cup while Naomi prepares to undock. The two argue about whether it qualifies as coffee.
Jex's genuine three-track interception trace reaches the working display. Naomi compares it to the exit end of the civilian route; there is no mystical knowledge or impossible foresight.
Naomi moves Sunlash out ahead of the first civilian skiff toward the threatened receiving end. The co-pilot follows without another explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Co-pilot
dialogueInline.text: It's coffee. It comes from a bean.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: So does castor oil. Wouldn't put it in my breakfast.

dialogueInline.speaker: Co-pilot
dialogueInline.text: Jex's trace. Three ships, all converging.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Tess is covering the launch. They're counting on us being late at the other end.

dialogueInline.speaker: Co-pilot
dialogueInline.text: We're not late.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Not yet. Bring us around. And throw that drink out before it eats the cup.

settingText: INT. SUNLASH — COCKPIT / EXT. DEPARTURE BERTH — DAY

summary: Billie holds her Ashfang crew with a vivid, probably true story about a stranger who bluffed an entire dock security office; the story is pleasurable in itself, not a coded battle plan.
panelPlan: In Ashfang Marauder's practical galley adjoining command, crew members share a rare decent meal while Billie balances on a bench. She begins an old story with intimate, confident relish.

Flashback inset contained within the spoken anecdote: a small frontier customs room; a severe woman in a spotless coat carries her own chair in and places it opposite an officer. No readable signs or invented proper labels.

Billie continues as the crew interrupt, delighted. The woman confidently pretends to be an inspector sent to inspect the inspectors, and a nervous staff gradually begin correcting their own books for her.

Back in Ashfang's galley, Billie reaches the absurd, believable payoff; her crew laugh, and one unconvinced listener tries a final question. A duty light flashes; Billie finishes the story before leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: There was a customs office on Vey's Landing. Five guards, two clerks, and a chief who'd arrested his own wife for bringing him lunch through the wrong door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: You were there?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I was trying to leave. Woman walks in carrying a chair. Not a weapon. A chair. Sets it opposite the chief and asks why his inspection is six hours late.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: Whose inspection?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: That's what he asked. She looked offended.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Told him headquarters had sent her to inspect his inspections. By noon he had every clerk digging through a year's accounts, apologizing for their handwriting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: What did she steal?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Nothing. She was delivering four crates of boots. They unloaded her ship while she sat in there criticizing their filing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: You're telling me they thanked her?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: The chief shook her hand. I watched him do it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: And who was she?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: A woman who didn't fancy paying docking fees. I bought her dinner.

settingText: INT. ASHFANG MARAUDER — GALLEY / COMMAND — DAY
directionInline: Billie's self-contained anecdote is an entertaining piece of character performance, not foreshadowing or a lesson about the battle. A brief, clearly recognizable imagined flashback may accompany it without creating readable signs, and must not be mistaken for currently occurring Tal Corvus action.

summary: Pike and the Broken Oath crew conduct a hilariously over-serious dispute about the ownership of a last piece of cake, showing charisma and vanity before the coming rescue tests him.
panelPlan: Inside Broken Oath's working mess adjacent to a modest camera-control station, Pike confronts a cook holding an empty serving tray. Nearby crew watch with the enjoyment of people who have heard his arguments before.
Pike insists that a cake's final slice belongs to the captain. The cook points out the captain already took the first slice, and another crew member offers an infuriatingly reasonable objection.
Pike attempts an elaborate defense of ceremonial privilege while the crew calmly dismantle his logic. No one is threatened or disciplined; this is familiar off-watch banter.
An officer at the open hatch announces the crossing schedule. Pike straightens his coat for a camera drone while the cook eats the missing final slice behind him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: There is a principle involved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cook
dialogueInline.text: You ate the first slice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: I tested the cake. That's command responsibility.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: Then you can confirm it was excellent and allow someone else the last one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: The last slice is ceremonial.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cook
dialogueInline.text: What ceremony?

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: I'm still developing that part.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: You've been developing it for three voyages.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Great institutions take time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Captain, the civilians are nearly ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Right. Cameras to the docking side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cook
dialogueInline.text: And somebody tell him we ran out of cake.

settingText: INT. BROKEN OATH — MESS / COMMAND ACCESS — DAY

summary: The refugees board and depart, carrying ordinary conversations into the skiffs; their private concerns make the imminent crossing intelligible without repeated tactical exposition.
panelPlan: Inside the civilian skiff, the mother tries to stow her heavy bag and discovers the stubborn old latch. Her daughter sits beside the mechanic and examines the tiny blank copy of her earlier ship drawing.
A civilian pilot completes ordinary mechanical checks. The neighbor jokes about the old kettle argument, and the mother finally joins the laughter as the engines begin to vibrate.
Across Tal Corvus, the certified green third-window markers illuminate for the first time. Gravefire draws the skiffs away from the berth; there is no magical glowing tunnel.

A wide, unambiguous composition establishes the crossing in one image: skiffs moving from Tal Corvus toward Auric, Tess's Gravefire beside them, Naomi's Sunlash ahead, and Deka's Thunderbreak outside the line. Hostile craft wait beyond the safe course.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Does the ship have a kitchen?

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: Not one you'd want to see.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: You'd know. You've got my kettle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: You're really going to carry that into space?

dialogueInline.speaker: Pilot
dialogueInline.text: Everybody seated, please. We're leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: There you go. We're moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: I can see the green lights.

settingText: INT. CIVILIAN SKIFF / EXT. TAL CORVUS THIRD-WINDOW ROUTE — DUSK
directionInline: This is the first active civilian transit; no earlier page has moved civilian skiffs through the green markers. Establish the simple spatial geography here and do not repeat it in full on later pages. The skiffs are individually varied working craft, not uniform fighter formations.

summary: Tess and Deka coordinate physical shelter for the departing civilians, revealing guarded mutual respect through concise, understandable operational exchange rather than jargon.
panelPlan: On Gravefire's compact repaired bridge, Tess sees Ashfang's associated skiffs edging too close to the civilian departures.
On Thunderbreak's disciplined bridge, Deka listens over an ordinary ship-to-ship channel while an officer marks how the cruiser can interpose armor without blocking the route.
A coherent exterior shows Thunderbreak's repaired armored flank slowly turning to shield civilian craft; Gravefire continues guiding them, with independent commands and no shared station controls.
Tess notices the big cruiser's guns remain dark. Her dry acknowledgement is restrained but recognizably hers; Deka remains attentive to the continuing risk.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Billie's crowding the families. One frightened pilot turns sideways and we'll have trouble.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: We'll place Thunderbreak between them. It won't be a fast turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I'd worry more if that ship started turning fast.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Our guns remain inactive. Keep the civilians close to Gravefire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I can use that. Thank you, Lieutenant.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Get them home, Captain.

settingText: INT. GRAVEFIRE / INT. THUNDERBREAK / EXT. THIRD-WINDOW ROUTE — DUSK
directionInline: Deka legally commands Thunderbreak, Tess commands Gravefire, and they coordinate only via an ordinary ship-to-ship channel. Preserve exact established hulls and Thunderbreak's prior damage.

summary: Naomi holds her position against a hostile approach and makes room for a disciplined but characterful argument with a nervous Verge wingman.
panelPlan: Sunlash holds the receiving side of the moving civilian line. The co-pilot spots an armed craft approaching from the direction predicted by Jex.
A Verge wingman reports being targeted and wants to break off to confront the attacker. Naomi listens rather than reflexively lecturing.
Naomi explains in direct human terms that pursuing would leave the incoming families alone. The wingman reluctantly swings back beside the civilian skiffs.
The attacker remains beyond the convoy, which continues toward Sunlash without a shot. Naomi's co-pilot glances at the terrible coffee still in the cockpit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Co-pilot
dialogueInline.text: There's the ship Jex marked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wingman
dialogueInline.text: They're holding a lock on us. Permission to answer it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: And leave three loaded skiffs to greet them alone?

dialogueInline.speaker: Wingman
dialogueInline.text: I don't like sitting here while they aim at us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Neither do I. Stay where those families can see you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Co-pilot
dialogueInline.text: The coffee's gone cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: It was dead when you poured it.

settingText: INT. SUNLASH COCKPIT / EXT. THIRD-WINDOW EXIT — DUSK

summary: Billie chooses an intimidating warning shot despite a subordinate's concern; she does not intend to hit refugees but knowingly creates a dangerous situation.
panelPlan: On Ashfang's functional bridge, Billie watches the civilian skiffs continue past her boundary. Her weapon officer warns that the refugee pilots are already making nervous corrections.
Billie hears Tess's defensive challenge over the common channel and resents being kept outside the crossing. She is impatient with an outcome she cannot control.
Billie authorizes one warning burst across empty space ahead of the tugs. The weapon officer hesitates a fraction before following a direct order.
External wide: the burst crosses clear space without striking any ship. A heavily loaded civilian pilot sees it and reacts before being able to judge its actual path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: The civilian tugs are tight enough together already.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: They think Abby drew a line and the rest of us disappeared.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Their pilots can't tell which direction our guns are pointed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: One burst ahead of them. Clear space, no hulls.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Captain—

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I said no hulls. Fire.

settingText: INT. ASHFANG MARAUDER — COMMAND / EXT. CORRIDOR EDGE — DUSK

summary: Billie's warning shot provokes two different civilian tugs into evasive mistakes; the danger follows clearly from frightened pilots, not a mysterious corridor phenomenon.
panelPlan: Interior of the first tug: its pilot sees the burst in the forward glass, jerks the controls, and loses a worn thruster. Freight shifts as alarms sound.
Another civilian tug veers in the opposite direction, crossing outside the route toward the fixed Fleet defensive boundary.
One tug drifts near sharp industrial debris; the other moves beyond the help of the nearest escort. Neither craft is hit by the warning burst.
Gravefire remains beside the families who stayed on course. Tess sees the two separated tugs and has to refuse an impossible attempt to chase both.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pilot
dialogueInline.text: That was across our bow!

dialogueInline.speaker: Passenger
dialogueInline.text: We're turning—

dialogueInline.speaker: Pilot
dialogueInline.text: I've lost thrust. I can't stop it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Both tugs are out. Gravefire can't leave the others.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Someone get to them.

settingText: INT. TWO CIVILIAN TUGS / EXT. THIRD-WINDOW ROUTE — CONTINUOUS

summary: Pike sees the stranded first tug and gives up his carefully staged public image to attempt a rescue his ship can actually perform.
panelPlan: Broken Oath's established camera drones seek its flattering broadside while a drift-disabled civilian tug hangs dangerously near debris, partly hidden behind the big Shard ship.
A working officer shows Pike the tug's actual danger. For a moment Pike watches his own camera image instead of the vessel.
Pike cuts off the show feed and orders a turn toward the tug. His crew react instantly, realizing the maneuver will put the ship into hostile fire.
Exterior: Broken Oath swings stern-first into the exposed approach, ugly rather than heroic; abandoned drones struggle to keep up.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Captain. The tug behind us lost its engines.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: How far?

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Too far for them. Close enough for us if we turn now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Then turn. Drop the camera feed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: We'll look terrible from that angle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: For once, I'm not asking how we look.

settingText: INT. BROKEN OATH — COMMAND / EXT. CORRIDOR RIM — CONTINUOUS

summary: A junior Fleet escort officer independently leaves formation to save the second civilian tug; Deka covers the gap without claiming the officer's choice was authorized.
panelPlan: Thunderbreak's bridge: Tactical sees the other drifting tug pass beyond the Fleet defensive screen. Deka listens to the junior escort captain on the working channel.
The officer aboard a smaller Fleet ship sees the tug's helpless crew and requests time that the route window cannot provide. Standing orders remain to hold station.
The junior officer makes the unauthorized turn before Deka can issue a command. A vulnerable gap opens between the remaining Fleet craft.
Deka refuses an offered offensive weapon option and orders Thunderbreak's shields and broad repaired hull to cover the opening. The response is disciplined, physical, and consequential.

dialogueInline.speaker: Junior Officer
dialogueInline.text: The second tug's drifting beyond us. They can't recover without a tow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: That escort is assigned to the screen. There's no release to leave it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Junior Officer
dialogueInline.text: I'm going after them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Ma'am, they're already turning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: I see it. Helm, cover the gap. No offensive fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: And the officer's departure?

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Record it accurately. Then help me bring them back.

settingText: INT. THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND / INT. FLEET ESCORT — CONTINUOUS
directionInline: Junior Fleet officer initiates breach independently before Deka orders a defensive cover; Deka owns the second decision. Venn is not present or in command. Thunderbreak's guns are inactive under Dominion's release restriction.

summary: Broken Oath physically recovers the first tug but has to sacrifice its relief pallet, choosing human life over a cargo supply that Auric urgently needs.
panelPlan: Broken Oath crosses the exposed hostile picket under fire while its grappling crew work a real mechanical tow connection toward the powerless civilian tug.
Pike and his officer watch the tow latch and the vulnerable civilians through a plain working window, not a cinematic heroic display.
The ship strains under the tow load; an essential relief grain pallet can be jettisoned to reduce mass and clear the threatened edge. The cook from the earlier argument is now helping the crew.
Pike orders the pallet released. The substantial freight drifts irretrievably away as Broken Oath begins hauling the tug.
Inside the rescued tug, a crew member confirms the line holds. Pike's crew work the tow in silence; Pike's cameras are no longer following him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: We're across the picket. They can hit us here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Can we get a line aboard?

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: If they hold steady another ten seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cook
dialogueInline.text: The tow's too heavy with that grain pallet. They loaded it for days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: I know who it's for.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: We can't keep both.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Cut the pallet. Save the crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Line's holding. We've got them.

settingText: INT. BROKEN OATH / EXT. HOSTILE PICKET — CONTINUOUS

summary: The second Fleet rescue and Gravefire's last exposed escort become one compact crosscut action sequence; Tess's ship sustains lasting radiator damage while Deka's screen stretches to cover the returning Fleet craft.
panelPlan: The junior Fleet escort attaches a believable towing line to the second disabled tug. The officer and civilian pilot exchange one concise acknowledgement.
Gravefire guides the remaining skiffs through a heat-washed segment of the physical crossing. The ship's established port radiator surfaces buckle, with no mystical energy effects.
On Gravefire, Tess chooses to use the last emergency cooling reserve rather than abandon the slowest skiff. Her crew moves immediately to protect the remaining propulsion and shield capacity.
On Thunderbreak, Deka keeps the shield gap covered while the junior escort brings its tug back; neither independently commanded rescue is transformed into a preapproved maneuver.
Wide exterior: the two rescues proceed separately, while damaged Gravefire continues beside the remaining convoy and Sunlash waits ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Junior Officer
dialogueInline.text: Tow is secure. Are your people all aboard?

dialogueInline.speaker: Pilot
dialogueInline.text: All aboard. Please move us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: Port radiator is buckling. The next heat pass could take cooling off-line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Use the reserve. We're not leaving the last skiff in this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Escort's coming back through the gap. We can still cover them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Hold it until they're clear.

settingText: INT. FLEET ESCORT / INT. GRAVEFIRE / INT. THUNDERBREAK — CONTINUOUS
directionInline: Maintain the cause and persistence of Gravefire's port radiator damage and depleted cooling reserve; this does not heal during later pages or Issue 5. Preserve independent Fleet officer, Deka, Pike and Tess responsibility.

summary: The skiffs and both rescued tugs survive the closing window; the civilian crossing completes in a legible visual sequence without repeating tactical assignments.
panelPlan: Sunlash receives the final ordinary civilian skiff. In its cockpit Naomi waits for a final head count rather than congratulating herself.
The junior Fleet escort arrives with the second tug as Thunderbreak maintains its stretched defensive cover; Broken Oath separately hauls the first tug toward Black Drift, freight pallet absent.
Gravefire clears the dangerous heat wash with its permanently scored port radiator; Tess watches the last skiff disappear beyond the exit beacons.
The certified green window closes only after all civilians are clear. The formerly crowded crossing empties; the ships return to their distinct sovereign stations.

dialogueInline.speaker: Co-pilot
dialogueInline.text: Last skiff is through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: And the two tugs?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Fleet escort has one. Pike has the other.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Tess, come on. Don't make us tow you as well.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I heard that. My radiators heard it too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Good. Then everybody gets to complain about something tomorrow.

settingText: EXT. CORRIDOR EXIT / INT. SUNLASH — NIGHT
directionInline: Do not unify the separate commands into a single Fleet or coalition chain of authority. The rescued tug hauled by Pike returns toward Black Drift; Auric receives refugee skiffs and has lost the relief grain pallet.

summary: Dominion and historian Selene examine unedited evidence of Deka's escort gap, the independent officer's disobedience, and the recovered civilians; their argument reveals temperaments rather than two slogans.
panelPlan: At the Relic Court, Dominion watches a precise recording of the junior officer's unauthorized turn while Selene stands at a separate review station with the complete event sequence.
Dominion stops the footage on the gap and asks Selene what might have happened had another escort followed. She refuses to falsify the risk.
Selene resumes the recording past the breach to show the tow and Deka physically covering the gap. She presses Dominion to include all the evidence in the record.
Dominion orders an actual review of the decision, not instant exoneration. Selene remains beside the recording after he leaves, turning it back to a rescued civilian's relieved face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: They left a guarded position without authorization.

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: Yes. The gap was real.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: If our other officers follow an example like that, the next convoy could be lost.

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: Then the inquiry needs that possibility and the people actually saved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: You think I intend to erase them?

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: I think this frame ends before they come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Keep the entire record. I want the officers heard before any finding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: That's all I asked.

settingText: INT. RELIC COURT — DOCUMENTARY REVIEW — NIGHT
directionInline: Deka remains the acting commander answerable for covering the breach, while the junior officer remains solely responsible for initiating an unauthorized turn. Selene's role is evidence-based historical analysis, not mystical interpretation.

summary: Tess comforts a frightened adult survivor and confronts Billie directly; the sisters' difficult relationships and Billie's consequences emerge without a fresh tactical briefing.
panelPlan: Inside a safely arriving skiff, an adult passenger gripping a seat watches battered Gravefire through a real comm display. Tess offers practical reassurance while continuing to work her bridge station.
The passenger tries a shaky joke that Tess answers dryly; the pilot settles the skiff into an ordinary landing approach.
On Gravefire, Tess looks at the scored radiator and opens a private ship-to-ship channel to Billie. They have enough history not to pretend the warning shot was harmless.
Billie answers from Ashfang. She hears how many people she frightened, but refuses Tess's implied claim to judge her. Tess breaks the channel to help her damaged ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Passenger
dialogueInline.text: Is your ship supposed to look like that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Not ideally. Your pilot's got you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Passenger
dialogueInline.text: That's comforting in a very specific way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: It's the best kind I have left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Your shot scattered two loaded tugs. You saw what happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I fired into empty space.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: There were people watching from a few meters away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: They're home, aren't they?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Other people made sure of that.

settingText: INT. CIVILIAN SKIFF / INT. GRAVEFIRE / INT. ASHFANG COMMS — NIGHT

summary: The Triarch emissary tries to make Billie attack independent Shard crop domes and lose local food autonomy; Billie refuses despite losing promised fuel, without erasing her wrongdoing.
panelPlan: Inside Ashfang's command deck, an ordinary Triarch emissary transmits a tactical packet showing independent Shard crop domes near Tal Corvus. Billie's weapons crew recognizes the farms.
The emissary explains with detached certainty that destroying agricultural independence will force those communities back onto controlled supply routes.
Billie realizes the threatened farms supply actual Shard families. The emissary offers a genuine price: fuel and access vanish if she refuses.
Billie personally clears the agricultural target from her command display. A plain fuel-allocation graphic goes inactive. Her crew can see she has made their lives harder.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: The farms survived. The people who own them will keep eating without our ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: That's usually what farms are for.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: Burn the domes. They'll have to buy from the routes we control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: My people work those fields.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: The fuel arrangement ends if you refuse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then it ends.

dialogueInline.speaker: Crewmate
dialogueInline.text: Captain, our next burn depends on that shipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I know. Clear the targets. We find fuel somewhere else.

settingText: INT. ASHFANG MARAUDER — COMMAND — NIGHT
directionInline: Billie does not become morally innocent after refusing the agricultural strike; she remains responsible for scattering the tugs. The Triarch are practical political actors, not supernatural authority.

summary: Survivors reach Auric and discover that arrival is both joyous and awkward: strangers become temporary neighbors in the freight hall where food should be unloaded.
panelPlan: At Auric's receiving dock, families step out of varied civilian skiffs onto a working floor marked by movable heater banks, not festive triumphal banners.
The girl spots a welcome volunteer carrying an improbable stack of bedding and asks whether the entire hall is meant for them. Her mother meets a skeptical local resident near the entrance.
The resident and Tal Corvus mechanic recognize a similar work habit and exchange a small practical joke while moving beds; the mother's anxious face finally relaxes.
Wide hall: new families take places on the freight floor while empty grain berths and cleared cargo spaces remain conspicuous. No one treats warm shelter as a permanent solution.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Is this where we live?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: It's where we sleep tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Neighbor
dialogueInline.text: Someone's going to complain about all these bags.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dockhand
dialogueInline.text: Someone already has. He left five minutes ago to find a bigger cart.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mechanic
dialogueInline.text: Now that's management I can support.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Where should we put our things?

dialogueInline.speaker: Dockhand
dialogueInline.text: Pick somewhere warm. We'll sort the rest in the morning.

settingText: INT. AURIC FREEPORT — HEATED FREIGHT HALL — NIGHT

summary: Naomi returns to Halev after the crossing; exhausted affection and a fleeting joke give way to the concrete grain shortage caused by Pike's lost pallet and a separate missing convoy.
panelPlan: At Auric's working flight desk, Naomi arrives with an exhausted co-pilot. Halev tries to offer her a drink from a pot that has clearly been warming far too long.
They exchange a familiar joke before Naomi reports every civilian safe, both tugs recovered, and Pike's missing grain pallet.
Halev steps into the crowded warm hall. The untouched blank space reserved for incoming relief cargo has become bedding, and the preexisting supply convoy still has not arrived.
A parent portions meager food for two children; Naomi and Halev fall quiet, realizing that the rescue solved an immediate emergency but not tomorrow's meals.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Coffee?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: That depends. Did your pilot make it or mine?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Neither. I did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then I'll risk it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They're all in. Both tugs recovered. Pike had to lose the grain pallet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: And the supply convoy still hasn't called.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Tell me what you need first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow morning, an honest count of what we've got.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I'll bring somebody who can count. You've made terrible coffee.

settingText: INT. AURIC FREEPORT — FLIGHT DESK / FREIGHT HALL — NIGHT

summary: At Black Drift, Pike comes home expecting applause but discovers that practical work holds his attention more urgently; preserve the silent, unadvertised change.
panelPlan: At Black Drift's dock, Broken Oath brings in the rescued civilian tug with a damaged tow and camera drones still trailing the ship. A real crowd, including friends of the rescued crew, begins cheering.
Pike emerges and instinctively raises an arm toward the waiting camera drone; his old smile starts to form.
Abby stands beside a dockhand wrestling with a twisted tow connector. A rescued person is having trouble with the steep gangway; the people, not a speech, hold Pike's gaze.
Pike lowers his arm and puts both hands on the tow connector beside the dockhand. The camera hangs awkwardly behind him while he works.
settingText: EXT. BLACK DRIFT — CIVILIAN DOCK — NIGHT
directionInline: The rescued tug's crew are specific individuals and Pike's change is behavior, not a speech. Keep this page silent and preserve the rescue damage and absent relief pallet.

summary: The Fear Mask prepares a manipulative release of authentic but incomplete footage, treating political interpretation as a weapon after the failed interdiction.
panelPlan: In a practical, secure Shadow Warrens recording room, a Triarch emissary reports that every evacuated civilian reached safety. The Fear Mask watches the unedited feed.
The full recording shows Billie's genuine warning shot, two panicked departures, the later unauthorized Fleet formation break, and the actual tugs recovered.
The Fear Mask instructs the emissary to stop the footage at the Fleet gap, before the rescues. Technicians mark the edit using ordinary apparatus without invented words.
The edited footage is prepared for distribution; the original remains physically intact, making the deception selective rather than a fabricated event.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: They made the crossing. The missing crews came back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: The shot is real. So is the break in the Fleet line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: And so are the rescues.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: End the public sequence before them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: People will think the convoy was abandoned.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear Mask
dialogueInline.text: They'll see what happened. They won't see how it ended.

settingText: INT. SHADOW WARRENS — TRIARCH RECORDING ROOM — NIGHT

summary: Naomi meets the mother and child again in Auric's temporary shelter. Their relaxed talk about ordinary belongings quietly exposes that nobody knows whether the family can unpack.
panelPlan: In Auric's temporarily heated freight hall, the mother carefully guards a dented old tin and a too-heavy bag. Her daughter copies the ships she saw on the crossing onto a blank scrap, adding Broken Oath.
Naomi approaches still wearing her Verge flight jacket and asks about the tin. The mother reveals an unglamorous memory rather than making a statement about exile.
The daughter wonders whether her new drawing belongs on a wall. The adults cannot answer whether they are staying, but Naomi refuses to make the uncertainty the child's responsibility tonight.
Naomi takes the heavy bag and carries it toward the family's makeshift sleeping space. The mother follows, holding the tin; the child stays close with her drawing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You carried that tin all the way from Tal Corvus?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: My husband's terrible biscuits. I kept telling him I'd throw them away. Never did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Are they still terrible?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: I wouldn't waste a good memory by tasting one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Can I put my ships on the wall?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Ask me in the morning, love.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Come on. I'll take the bag.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: It's not very heavy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: That's what strong people always say.

settingText: INT. AURIC FREEPORT — TEMPORARY SHELTER — NIGHT

summary: The silent closing montage contrasts real rescue acclaim, unresolved Fleet review, hungry receiving halls, Gravefire's persistent damage, and the family's uncertainty, ending on an empty food container beside a sleeping child.
panelPlan: At Black Drift, Pike's crowd and drones keep recording while the recovered tug rests on its damaged tow fittings.
Fleet officers review the unauthorized turn and Deka's shielding maneuver as an open disciplinary matter, rather than declaring an immediate verdict.
At Auric, dock workers stand beside the conspicuously absent grain pallet's unloading position, now swallowed by temporary bedding.
Shard mechanics touch the scored port radiator of Gravefire, assessing repairs that cannot be done tonight.
In a quiet final close-up, the girl sleeps beside a warm heater, her ship sketch nearby, while the mother puts an empty food container aside for tomorrow. No narration or speech.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT / THUNDERBREAK / AURIC / GRAVEFIRE — AFTERMATH
directionInline: Final page has no readable dialogue, captions, interface writing, memorial inscriptions or political slogans. The child drawing must match its established evolution; Gravefire's radiator damage persists.
